sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: Study of **Common Diseases** (सामान्य रोग), pathogens, transmission modes, symptoms, prevention, and treatment.
Core segment of **General Science** tested continuously in all UPSSSC PET examination shifts.
Applied directly in questions regarding **Infectious Disease**, deficiency disorders, and public health schemes.
Aspirants preparing for **UPSSSC PET** aiming to score full marks in the General Science section.
Carries **2-3 guaranteed marks** in the PET exam via direct questions on vectors, causative agents, and vaccines.
Classification into **communicable** and **non-communicable** diseases, viral/bacterial/protozoal/fungal categorizations.
High-yield static GK topic requiring precise recall of scientific names, deficiency vitamins, and immunization schedules.
Includes **Bacteria**, **Viruses**, **Protozoa**, **Fungi**, and **Helminths** responsible for human morbidity.

items.title: Bacterial Diseases and Causative Agents
items.content:
• **Tuberculosis (TB):** Caused by **Mycobacterium tuberculosis**; affects lungs; BCG vaccine used for prevention.
• **Typhoid:** Caused by **Salmonella typhi**; diagnosed via **Widal test**; affects intestines.
• **Cholera:** Caused by **Vibrio cholerae**; leads to severe acute watery diarrhea.
• **Diphtheria:** Affects mucous membranes of throat and nose; **DPT vaccine** provides immunity.
• **Tetanus:** Caused by **Clostridium tetani**; affects nervous system; also called **Lockjaw**.
• **Mnemonic for Bacterial Diseases:** **" पंडित का न्यू का, गोटी छिट, प्लेन है "** (Pandi ka New ka, Goti Chhit, Plain hai) -> Plaque, Diphtheria, Typhoid, Kushi(Leprosy), Pneumonia, Tetanus, Gonorrhea, Cholera, Tuberculosis.

items.title: Viral Diseases and Transmission Modes
items.content:
• **Rabies (Hydrophobia):** Caused by **Rhabdovirus** through infected dog/animal bites; affects central nervous system.
• **AIDS:** Caused by **Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV)**; targets **CD4+ T-lymphocytes**; tested via **ELISA** and **Western Blot**.
• **Polio:** Enterovirus affecting spinal cord, leading to paralysis; **Salk vaccine** (injectable) and **Sabin vaccine** (oral).
• **Dengue:** Transmitted by **Aedes aegypti** mosquito; causes sudden high fever and drop in **platelet count**.
• **Mnemonic for Viral Diseases:** **" रेखा हमेंहिट करके पो पीछे छोड़ गई "** (Rekha Humein Hit karke Po pichhe chhod gayi) -> Rabies, Khasra, Herpes, Meningitis, Hepatitis, Polio, Chickenpox, Chhola(Smallpox), AIDS, Dengue, Influenza.

items.title: Protozoal and Fungal Infections
items.content:
• **Malaria:** Caused by **Plasmodium** species (vivax, falciparum); transmitted by female **Anopheles mosquito**; treated with **Quinine** (derived from cinchona bark).
• **Amoebiasis (Dysentery):** Caused by **Entamoeba histolytica**; transmitted through contaminated food and water.
• **Sleeping Sickness:** Caused by **Trypanosoma**; transmitted by **Tsetse fly**.
• **Kala-azar (Leishmaniasis):** Caused by **Leishmania donovani**; transmitted by **Sandfly**.
• **Ringworm (Dermatophytosis):** Fungal infection caused by **Microsporum**, **Trichophyton**, and **Epidermophyton**.
• **Mnemonic for Protozoal Diseases:** **" पापा काम पे सोते हैं "** (Papa Kaam Pe Sote Hain) -> Pa (Pyorrhea), Pa (Kala-azar), Ka (Malaria), M (Amoebic dysentery), Pe (Sleeping sickness).

items.title: Deficiency Diseases and Vitamin Disorders
items.content:
• **Vitamin A (Retinol):** Deficiency causes **Night Blindness** (Nyctalopia) and Xerophthalmia.
• **Vitamin B1 (Thiamine):** Deficiency causes **Beriberi**.
• **Vitamin B3 (Niacin):** Deficiency causes **Pellagra** (characterized by 4 Ds: Dermatitis, Diarrhea, Dementia, Death).
• **Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid):** Deficiency causes **Scurvy** (bleeding gums).
• **Vitamin D (Calciferol):** Deficiency causes **Rickets** in children and **Osteomalacia** in adults.
• **Vitamin K (Phylloquinone):** Deficiency causes non-clotting of blood leading to **hemorrhage**.

items.title: Genetic and Chromosomal Disorders
items.content:
• **Down Syndrome:** Trisomy of **Chromosome 21**; causes mental retardation and distinct facial features.
• **Turner Syndrome:** Monosomy of sex chromosomes (**45, XO**); affects females, leading to sterile short stature.
• **Klinefelter Syndrome:** Presence of extra X chromosome (**47, XXY**); affects males, leading to gynecomastia and sterility.
• **Hemophilia:** X-linked recessive bleeding disorder; also called **Bleeder's Disease** (royal disease).
• **Color Blindness:** Inability to distinguish between red and green colors; X-linked recessive genetic trait.

items.definition: Remember **"MAD"** -> **M**alaria (Anopheles), **A**edes (Dengue/Chikungunya/Zika), **D**emodex/Culex (Japanese Encephalitis).
Remember **"CHOTA"** -> **C**holera, **H**epatitis A, **O**ther dysenteries, **T**yphoid, **A**moebiasis.
Remember **"WET" is wrong, it's "KDAE"** -> **K, D, A, E** are fat-soluble vitamins, while **B and C** are water-soluble.
Always check vectors: Bacteria respond to **antibiotics**, whereas viruses only respond to **antivirals** and preventative **vaccines**.
Remember **"HOC"** -> **H**emophilia, **O**ptic (Color Blindness), **C**alico cat syndrome; all are X-linked recessive.
Link **Widal** strictly with **Typhoid** and **ELISA** with **HIV/AIDS** to avoid exam confusion.
Students often confuse **Anopheles** (malaria) with **Aedes** (dengue). Remember: Female Anopheles causes malaria, Aedes aegypti causes dengue.
Thinking antibiotics cure viral infections like common cold or polio. **Antibiotics only kill bacteria**, never viruses.
Confusing Beriberi (Vitamin B1) with Pellagra (Vitamin B3). **Thiamine** deficiency causes Beriberi; **Niacin** deficiency causes Pellagra.
Confusing Trisomy 21 with Turner Syndrome. Down syndrome is **Trisomy 21**, Turner syndrome is monosomy of sex chromosomes (**45, XO**).
Assuming rabies is bacterial due to animal bites. Rabies is caused by a **Rhabdovirus**, not bacteria.
Confusing BCG with Polio drops. **BCG** is administered for Tuberculosis, whereas **OPV (Oral Polio Vaccine)** is for Polio.
Infectious diseases spread via pathogens (bacteria, virus), while non-infectious diseases arise from genetics, lifestyle, or deficiencies (e.g., diabetes, cancer).
Causative agents for Typhoid (**Salmonella typhi**), Cholera (**Vibrio cholerae**), and Tuberculosis (**Mycobacterium tuberculosis**).
Causative agents for AIDS (**HIV**), Rabies (**Rhabdovirus**), and Polio (**Enterovirus**).
Includes Malaria transmitted by **female Anopheles mosquito** and Sleeping Sickness by **Tsetse fly**.
Ringworm caused by dermatophytes (**Microsporum**, **Trichophyton**).
**Widal test** for typhoid, **ELISA** for HIV, and **Papanicolaou (Pap) smear** for cervical cancer screening.
**Edward Jenner** discovered the smallpox vaccine, establishing the foundation of immunology and vaccination.
Lack of Vitamin C causes **Scurvy**, Vitamin D causes **Rickets**, and Iron causes **Anemia**.
**Down Syndrome** involves 47 chromosomes with trisomy 21; **Klinefelter** features 47, XXY.
Preventing stagnant water stops mosquito breeding, mitigating malaria, dengue, and chikungunya outbreaks.

upscNotes.content: UPSSSC PET frequently asks matching questions pairing diseases with their respective vectors or diagnostic tests. Memorize the exact pairs from the data table.
Focus heavily on Vitamin deficiency names (chemical names like Retinol, Thiamine, Ascorbic Acid) as at least one question is standard in the PET science section.
Questions often trick students by stating antibiotics cure viral flu. Remember that viral diseases require vaccines or antivirals, not antibiotics.
Do not confuse the vector names: Anopheles mosquito for Malaria vs Aedes aegypti for Dengue. UPSSSC often swaps these in multiple-choice options.

keyTakeaways: Diseases are broadly classified into infectious (communicable) and non-infectious (non-communicable) categories.
Bacterial infections like typhoid and cholera are treated with antibiotics and diagnosed via specific tests like Widal.
Viral infections like rabies and AIDS require preventive vaccines or management therapies, as antibiotics are ineffective.
Protozoal diseases like malaria are vector-borne, requiring mosquito eradication and anti-malarial drugs like quinine.
Vitamin and mineral deficiencies lead to well-defined clinical disorders such as scurvy, rickets, and night blindness.
Genetic disorders like Down syndrome and Hemophilia are inherited and result from chromosomal aberrations or mutant genes.
